system.name: IronSync
system.one_liner: a methodology and toolkit for automated modular reasoning about complex concurrent systems by sharding a global state machine across fine-grained locks

content.subject: one DoTransfer(A,B,$7) execution tracking ghost shard values against physical heap values through locks and an atomic ghost transition

elements.name: Unlocked Heap
elements.role: shared heap; unlocked accounts' ghost/physical pairs live here when not held by a thread

elements.name: Thread 1
elements.role: a second thread whose account C is never touched by the pictured transfer

elements.name: Thread 2
elements.role: the thread executing the pictured DoTransfer(A,B,$7) call

elements.name: Client
elements.role: issues the txfr request and receives the ack

elements.name: global view
elements.role: (b) the GSM's single abstract state, one ghost shard set with no physical counterpart

elements.role: legend: dashed cyan box style denotes a ghost (specification-level) value

elements.name: physical

elements.role: account A's ghost/physical value pair; moves between Unlocked Heap and Thread 2 as it is locked/unlocked, changing from 9 to 2

elements.name: B
elements.role: account B's ghost/physical value pair; moves the same way, changing from 1 to 8

elements.role: account C's ghost/physical value pair; stays in Thread 1 throughout, constant at 1

relations.what: client requests transfer of $7 from A to B
Thread 2 acquires lock A, gaining its ghost shard and physical pointer
Thread 2 acquires lock B the same way
physical A is decremented from 9 to 2 (debit A)
physical B is incremented from 1 to 8 (credit B)
ghost A atomically jumps to 2, matching the GSM's one global step
ghost B atomically jumps to 8, matching the GSM's one global step
both accounts' now-consistent ghost/physical pairs return to the shared heap (unlock A, unlock B)
Thread 2 replies once the transfer is complete (ack txfr)

panels.label: t0: initial
panels.differs: before any action: A:9/B:1 both in Unlocked Heap, C:1 in Thread 1, no locks held

panels.label: after lock A, lock B
panels.differs: A and B's ghost/physical pairs have moved into Thread 2's row; both still read 9 and 1

panels.label: after debit A, credit B
panels.differs: physical values change to A:2, B:8 while the ghost values still read A:9, B:1

panels.label: ghost transition (instantaneous)
panels.differs: ghost values atomically jump to A:2, B:8, matching the global-view GSM's single atomic transition

panels.label: after unlock A, unlock B, ack txfr
panels.differs: A and B's now-consistent pairs return to the Unlocked Heap and Thread 2 acknowledges the client

steps.what: client requests transfer of $7 from A to B
physical A is decremented from 9 to 2
physical B is incremented from 1 to 8
ghost shards for A and B atomically jump to 2 and 8, matching the GSM's one global step
both accounts' now-consistent pairs return to the shared heap
Thread 2 acknowledges completion to the client

values.what: each account's ghost and physical value, shown numerically at every lifeline crossing
values.result_cells: dashed cyan boxes show the ghost value, solid yellow boxes show the physical value, both labelled with the account name and current numeric balance

content.key_idea: As Thread 2 executes one $7 transfer under separate A/B locks, the physical balances update first and the ghost (specification) values catch up atomically in one instantaneous step that exactly matches the GSM's single global transition.
content.reading_order: left to right along (a)'s time axis: request, lock A, lock B, debit A, credit B, the instantaneous ghost transition, unlock A/B, ack; then (b)'s aligned global view

yellow fill of solid physical-value boxes (e.g. the solid 'A:9' boxes)
light-grey banding alternating between the Unlocked Heap / Thread 1 / Thread 2 / Client lanes
pale peach fill of the lock A / lock B / unlock A / unlock B action ovals
pale mauve fill of the debit A / credit B ovals and the req/ack rounded end-caps

style.stroke: thin black outlines; dashed teal outline specifically for ghost-value boxes, solid black for physical-value boxes
style.arrows: thin black curved arrows linking a value box to its next position/state; two short arrows in the global-view row marking the atomic A/B jump
style.font: sans (DejaVu Sans), 6-6.5pt, small bold digits on changed values

encoding.color_means: cyan/dashed = ghost (specification) value; yellow/solid = physical (implementation) value; grey banding separates the Unlocked Heap / Thread 1 / Thread 2 / Client lanes
encoding.line_style_means: dashed outline marks a ghost-value box, solid outline marks a physical-value box; a hatched vertical band marks the instantaneous ghost-transition instant
encoding.state_means: before/after is told apart by column position along the time axis and by which lane (Unlocked Heap vs Thread 2) currently holds a value pair
encoding.marker_means: bold text on a value (e.g. 'A:2') marks that this is the instruction where the value just changed
encoding.emphasis: the hatched 'instantaneous' band isolates the single ghost-transition instant so it visually cannot be confused with the surrounding gradual physical updates
reusable_patterns: a swimlane timeline where a specification-level (ghost) copy and an implementation-level (physical) copy of the same value are drawn as paired boxes that travel together, with one isolated instant where the ghost jumps to re-sync
weaknesses: many near-identical small boxes across 8+ time columns make it easy to lose track of which column corresponds to which named action without following the ovals carefully

regardless of low-level thread interleaving, from GSM’s global perspective, the state advances through a sequence of atomic global transitions

summary: This figure from IronSync's core methodology section shows one invocation of the DoTransfer method as Thread 2 moves $7 from account A to B. Along a time-in-instructions axis, dashed cyan boxes (ghost values) and solid yellow boxes (physical values) for A, B, and C move between the Unlocked Heap, Thread 2, and Client lanes as Thread 2 locks A, locks B, debits A's physical value from 9 to 2, and credits B's physical value from 1 to 8. A hatched 'instantaneous' band marks the ghost transition, where both ghost values atomically jump to match the already-updated physical values, before Thread 2 unlocks A and B and acknowledges the client. The aligned (b) global view shows the same single atomic jump in the GSM's abstract state, tying the concrete execution to the abstract proof.
summary_zh: 该图展示IronSync中一次DoTransfer($7, A到B)的执行：沿时间轴，虚线青色的ghost值与实心黄色的physical值随线程2加锁A、加锁B、扣A、贷B移动；在灰色斜纹的瞬时ghost transition处两者原子跳变到新值后解锁并应答，(b)全局视图同步展示这一原子跳变。
notes: Added 'walkthrough' as a secondary group alongside the prior 'evolution': the eight named action ovals (lock A, lock B, debit A, credit B, ghost transition, unlock A, unlock B, ack txfr) trace one request through the structure in order via labelled arrows, matching the documented evolution+walkthrough overlap category. content.panels collapses the many fine-grained per-instruction time columns into 5 representative states (matching the schema's convention of describing the semantic evolution frames rather than the index's raw (a)/(b) panel count of 2, which is kept in layout.panels).
